In this study, SC Ni-based superalloys with different volume fractions of γ ′ phase and four corresponding thermal exposure times are selected for investigation.
in superalloys with φ = 30 %, γ ′ phase appears predominantly as uniformly dispersed spherical particles within the matrix phase;
in superalloys with φ = 60 %, the γ ′ phase mainly exhibits blocky or lath-like morphology with a denser distribution.

for superalloys with higher volume fraction of γ ′ phase ( φ = 60 %), the XRD pattern of the unexposed superalloys (i.e., HV-T0 alloy) likewise exhibits only the (111) and (200) diffraction peaks. However, an additional (110) diffraction peak gradually appears after thermal exposure, alongside the original peaks, indicating the precipitation of TCP phases.
